claims.title: Martyrdom of Saint Peter
claims.summary: According to tradition the apostle Peter was martyred in Rome during the persecution under Nero and buried on the Vatican Hill beside the circus, around 64 CE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-64-martyrdom-of-saint-peter, claim TL:VAT:event:64:martyrdom-of-saint-peter, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Trophy of Gaius marks the grave
claims.summary: About a century after Peter's death a small funerary monument, later known as the Trophy of Gaius, was built over the burial site and became a place of veneration.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-160-the-trophy-of-gaius-marks-the-grave, claim TL:VAT:event:160:the-trophy-of-gaius-marks-the-grave, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constantine builds Old St Peter's Basilica
claims.summary: The emperor Constantine raised a great basilica over the traditional tomb of Peter on the Vatican Hill, enclosing the shrine and making the site the chief sanctuary of Western Christendom.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-330-constantine-builds-old-st-peter-s-basilica, claim TL:VAT:event:330:constantine-builds-old-st-peter-s-basilica, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The bishops of Rome and apostolic succession
claims.summary: The popes were regarded as successors of Peter as bishops of Rome, a claim founded on the doctrine of apostolic succession that linked their authority to the apostle buried at the Vatican.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-380-the-bishops-of-rome-and-apostolic-succession, claim TL:VAT:event:380:the-bishops-of-rome-and-apostolic-succession, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Donation of Pepin creates the Papal States
claims.summary: After Pepin the Short forced the Lombards to surrender their conquests, he restored the lands of central Italy to the pope, creating the Papal States and the basis of papal temporal power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-756-the-donation-of-pepin-creates-the-papal-states, claim TL:VAT:event:756:the-donation-of-pepin-creates-the-papal-states, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Avignon papacy
claims.summary: The popes moved their residence to Avignon in France, where seven popes ruled for nearly seventy years away from Rome.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1309-the-avignon-papacy, claim TL:VAT:event:1309:the-avignon-papacy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gregory XI returns the papacy to Rome
claims.summary: Pope Gregory XI brought the papacy back to Rome from Avignon, against French opposition, ending the Avignon period.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1377-gregory-xi-returns-the-papacy-to-rome, claim TL:VAT:event:1377:gregory-xi-returns-the-papacy-to-rome, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Western Schism
claims.summary: Rival popes in Rome and Avignon divided the Church for four decades until the Council of Constance restored a single papacy in 1417.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1378-the-western-schism, claim TL:VAT:event:1378:the-western-schism, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Sistine Chapel completed
claims.summary: Built under Pope Sixtus IV, the Sistine Chapel was consecrated in 1483; it became the place where cardinals meet in conclave to elect the pope.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1483-the-sistine-chapel-completed, claim TL:VAT:event:1483:the-sistine-chapel-completed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First stone of the new Saint Peter's
claims.summary: Pope Julius II laid the foundation stone of an entirely new Saint Peter's Basilica to replace the failing fourth-century church; it was completed in 1626.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1506-first-stone-of-the-new-saint-peter-s, claim TL:VAT:event:1506:first-stone-of-the-new-saint-peter-s, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Michelangelo paints the Sistine ceiling
claims.summary: Commissioned by Julius II, Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel between 1508 and 1512, one of the supreme achievements of Renaissance art.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1508-michelangelo-paints-the-sistine-ceiling, claim TL:VAT:event:1508:michelangelo-paints-the-sistine-ceiling, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Origins of the Vatican Museums
claims.summary: The Vatican Museums trace their founding to 1506, when Julius II displayed the newly excavated ancient sculpture of the Laocoon, beginning the papal collections.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1506-origins-of-the-vatican-museums, claim TL:VAT:event:1506:origins-of-the-vatican-museums, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kingdom of Italy claims Rome
claims.summary: The new Kingdom of Italy, proclaimed in 1861, regarded Rome as its capital, leaving the pope's remaining territory protected only by a French garrison.

sources.label: Italy: The acquisition of Venetia and Rome

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1861-the-kingdom-of-italy-claims-rome, claim TL:VAT:event:1861:the-kingdom-of-italy-claims-rome, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The capture of Rome
claims.summary: Italian troops breached the walls at the Porta Pia and took Rome, ending more than a thousand years of papal temporal rule and completing the unification of Italy.

sources.label: Italy: The acquisition of Venetia and Rome

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1870-the-capture-of-rome, claim TL:VAT:event:1870:the-capture-of-rome, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pius IX, 'prisoner in the Vatican'
claims.summary: Refusing to accept the loss of Rome, Pope Pius IX withdrew into the Vatican and declared himself a prisoner, a position his successors held until 1929.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1871-pius-ix-prisoner-in-the-vatican, claim TL:VAT:event:1871:pius-ix-prisoner-in-the-vatican, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Roman Question
claims.summary: For nearly six decades the popes refused to recognise the Italian state's seizure of Rome, leaving the church-state dispute known as the Roman Question unresolved.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1874-the-roman-question, claim TL:VAT:event:1874:the-roman-question, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Signing of the Lateran Treaty
claims.summary: The Holy See and Italy signed the Lateran Treaty, signed by Mussolini for Italy and Cardinal Gasparri for the papacy, recognising the Holy See's sovereignty and creating the State of Vatican City.

sources.label: How the Vatican Became a Country

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1929-signing-of-the-lateran-treaty, claim TL:VAT:event:1929:signing-of-the-lateran-treaty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The State of Vatican City comes into being
claims.summary: With the exchange of ratifications on 7 June 1929 the State of Vatican City formally came into existence as an independent sovereign state of about 44 hectares.

sources.label: How the Vatican Became a Country

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1929-the-state-of-vatican-city-comes-into-being, claim TL:VAT:event:1929:the-state-of-vatican-city-comes-into-being, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Roman Question resolved
claims.summary: The Lateran Treaty ended the nearly sixty-year dispute over the popes' loss of Rome, reconciling the papacy to the Italian state in return for a sovereign territory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1929-the-roman-question-resolved, claim TL:VAT:event:1929:the-roman-question-resolved, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Wartime neutrality and the liberation of Rome
claims.summary: Vatican City kept to neutrality under Pius XII during the Second World War; though Rome was occupied and then liberated by the Allies on 4 June 1944, the Vatican itself was not occupied.

sources.label: Pius XII: World War II and the Holocaust

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1944-wartime-neutrality-and-the-liberation-of-rome, claim TL:VAT:event:1944:wartime-neutrality-and-the-liberation-of-rome, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Second Vatican Council
claims.summary: Opened by John XXIII on 11 October 1962 in Saint Peter's and concluded under Paul VI in 1965, Vatican II reformed the worship, self-understanding and outward relations of the Roman Catholic Church.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1962-the-second-vatican-council, claim TL:VAT:event:1962:the-second-vatican-council, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Holy See becomes a UN permanent observer
claims.summary: The Holy See established a Permanent Observer Mission to the United Nations in 1964, choosing observer status to preserve its neutrality, distinct from the territory of Vatican City State.

sources.label: The Holy See Celebrates Years as Permanent Observer to the United Nations
sources.publisher: Permanent Observer Mission of the Holy See to the UN

sources.label: Diplomatic Relations of the Holy See
sources.publisher: Permanent Observer Mission of the Holy See to the UN

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1964-the-holy-see-becomes-a-un-permanent-observer, claim TL:VAT:event:1964:the-holy-see-becomes-a-un-permanent-observer, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Vatican City inscribed as a World Heritage Site
claims.summary: UNESCO inscribed the entire State of Vatican City as a World Heritage Site, recognising Saint Peter's, the Sistine Chapel and the Vatican Museums as a cultural patrimony of universal value.

sources.label: Vatican City (World Heritage List, no. 286, inscribed 1984)
Historic Centre of Rome and the Holy See properties enjoying extraterritorial rights

claims.title: Diplomatic relations with the United States
claims.summary: The United States and the Holy See established full diplomatic relations on 10 January 1984, more than a century after the loss of the Papal States had ended earlier ties.

sources.label: Holy See — Countries
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian (history.state.gov)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Vatican City: From the tomb of an apostle to the world's smallest state: the long story of the popes' temporal power.", terralore.co/country/VAT/chronicle#ev-1984-diplomatic-relations-with-the-united-states, claim TL:VAT:event:1984:diplomatic-relations-with-the-united-states, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
